title: ELYS Life to Host Private Launch Event in Dubai
excerpt: ELYS Life will host a private launch event at Wellth by Medcare in Dubai on July 4, introducing its AI-powered nervous-system OS and personalized longevity mentor to a curated circle of founders, investors, doctors, wellness leaders, media, and strategic partners.
content:
**Dubai, UAE — July 4, 2026 —** ELYS Life, an AI-powered personalized health and longevity platform founded by Renat Mansurov, will host an intimate private launch event at Wellth by Medcare in Dubai.

Wellth is an integrative medicine and wellness hub launched by Aster DM Healthcare and managed by Medcare, offering services across sleep improvement, anti-ageing, regenerative medicine consultation, preventive screening, and other wellness-focused areas.

The private event will combine Mansurov’s birthday celebration with the official introduction of ELYS Life, bringing together 47 carefully selected VIP guests, including founders, investors, doctors, wellness leaders, media representatives, and strategic partners.

ELYS Life is being developed in the UAE as an AI nervous-system OS and personalized longevity mentor designed to support people in improving sleep, reducing stress and anxiety, managing panic-related signals, increasing energy, enhancing recovery, and optimizing overall human performance through personalized daily guidance.

> “The future of health will not be another dashboard,” said Renat Mansurov, Founder of ELYS Life. “People do not need more fragmented data. They need an intelligent system that understands their sleep, stress, recovery, panic signals, lifestyle, and habits — and gives them the right protocol at the right moment. That is what we are building with ELYS Life.”

The platform reflects a growing global shift toward preventive health, AI-powered wellness, nervous-system regulation, and individualized lifestyle optimization. The long-term vision of ELYS Life is to become an AI operating system for proactive health and longevity: a personal intelligence layer that helps people move from reactive healthcare to daily prevention, recovery, emotional balance, and performance.

The private gathering will serve as the first public introduction of the ELYS Life vision in Dubai and will mark the beginning of the brand’s Founding Circle — a select community of early supporters, partners, and advisors.

title: MENA Blockchain Week 2026 Concludes: How Dubai's First City-Wide Blockchain Initiative Drew 5,000+ Attendees Across 40+ Events
excerpt: MENA Blockchain Week 2026 brought together 5,000+ attendees, 100+ speakers, and 40+ events across Dubai, turning the city into a decentralized platform for blockchain, AI, digital assets, regulation, community, and institutional collaboration.
content:
## MENA Blockchain Week 2026: How Dubai Became a Citywide Blockchain Venue

MENA Blockchain Week 2026 has concluded its first edition in Dubai, positioning itself as the region’s first decentralized, citywide blockchain initiative.

Held with a Day 0 summit on May 14 and seven themed days from May 18 to 24, the initiative brought together more than 5,000 attendees, 100+ speakers, 40+ events, 1,000+ represented companies, and more than 30 partners across multiple venues in the city.

Unlike a traditional conference built around one main hall, MENA Blockchain Week turned Dubai itself into the venue. The format connected summits, private meetings, community gatherings, workshops, institutional sessions, ecosystem events, and partner-led activations under one shared identity.

### Dubai as a Blockchain City

The first edition reflected Dubai’s broader role as one of the global centers for blockchain, digital assets, AI, and emerging financial infrastructure.

The initiative was supported by Dubai Business Events, the official convention bureau of Dubai operating under the Department of Economy & Tourism, and was aligned with Dubai’s D33 economic agenda.

Participation included regulators, exchanges, ecosystem builders, financial institutions, infrastructure companies, and Web3 communities, with organizations such as VARA, Binance, Coinbase, Polygon, Stellar Development Foundation, Google, Bitpanda, Dubai Blockchain Center, DMCC Crypto Centre, Dubai Digital Asset Association, MENA Fintech Association, UAE Blockchain & AI Association, and others represented across the week.

### MENA Blockchain Week 2026 by the Numbers

MENA Blockchain Week 2026 gathered:

* 40+ events across Dubai
* 5,000+ attendees
* 100+ speakers
* 1,000+ represented companies
* 30+ partners
* 10M+ total reach
* 8.4M social reach
* 1.1M+ web reach
* 1,600+ mentions
* 99% positive sentiment
* 522 influencers and media voices
* 15K+ social interactions
* Coverage across 15+ publications

The audience was strongly business-focused: 57% of attendees were senior decision-makers, including founders, C-level executives, directors, and above.

The event also had a clear regional base with global interest. According to the organizers, 89% of the audience was UAE-based, 11% international, with attendees representing more than 40 nationalities and online interest coming from more than 90 countries.

### The Ecosystem That Chose to Build

MENA Blockchain Week 2026 arrived at a time when global markets were still facing uncertainty. Instead of slowing down, Dubai’s blockchain and digital asset ecosystem chose to organize, gather, and build.

The initiative showed a clear shift in the industry: the conversation is no longer only about speculation, tokens, or short-term market cycles. The focus is moving toward infrastructure, regulation, security, stablecoins, tokenization, AI, payments, community, and institutional adoption.

This made the week not only an event, but also a signal of maturity for the regional ecosystem.

### Why Dubai: Regulation, Capital, and Institutional Alignment

Dubai’s position in the blockchain industry is built on a combination of regulatory clarity, institutional support, international capital, and a strong inflow of talent.

MENA Blockchain Week reflected this structure. The initiative operated within Dubai’s regulated market environment, with participation from the Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority and other institutional stakeholders.

The format also distributed value across the city: organizers, venues, community partners, associations, government-linked entities, exchanges, founders, and investors all played a role in shaping the week.

### Day 0: The Summit Before the Week

Before the public program began, MENA Blockchain Week opened with a private Day 0 summit on May 14.

The Community Resilience Summit took place at Dubai Founders HQ, 25H Hotel One Central, and gathered regulators, founders, institutional investors, policymakers, and ecosystem leaders.

The purpose of the summit was to set the strategic tone for the week and discuss what the region’s next chapter in blockchain, AI, and digital assets should look like.

Speakers and participants included representatives from VARA, Dubai Blockchain Center, Binance, Bitpanda, Dubai Digital Asset Association, Middle East Stablecoin Association, SNXS, Hadron Founders Club, and other ecosystem organizations.

### Seven Themed Days Across the Digital Economy

After Day 0, the public program unfolded through seven themed days.

### Day 1: Builders & Community

The first day focused on builders and community, setting the tone for the week around one core idea: ecosystems are built by people who show up consistently.

The day highlighted community infrastructure, collaboration, and the importance of long-term participation in emerging technology sectors.

### Day 2: AI & Blockchain

The second day focused on the intersection of AI and blockchain.

The agenda explored automation, compute infrastructure, accountability, and the question of what happens when machines begin to play a larger role in financial systems and digital operations.

### Day 3: Stablecoins, Payments & Banking

The third day moved into one of the most important areas of the digital asset economy: stablecoins, payments, banking, and institutional capital flows.

Discussions focused on cross-border payment rails, regulated digital asset infrastructure, and the growing role of stablecoins in financial systems.

### Day 4: Regulation, Security & Compliance

The fourth day centered on regulation, security, custody, and compliance.

The program reflected one of the most important realities of the blockchain industry today: mass adoption depends not only on innovation, but also on trust, safety, licensing, and clear market rules.

### Day 5: RWA & Tokenization

The fifth day focused on real-world asset tokenization and stablecoin infrastructure.

A closed-door stablecoin track brought together organizations such as the Middle East Stablecoin Association, DMCC Crypto Centre, Dubai Digital Asset Association, and other digital asset leaders.

### Day 6: Creators Day & Workshop

The sixth day introduced a more practical and creator-focused dimension.

Workshops, masterclasses, and hands-on sessions explored AI, creator skills, and the tools that are changing how individuals and teams build, communicate, and scale.

### Day 7: Trading & Exchanges

The final themed day focused on trading, exchanges, Web3 communities, and AI tools.

It reflected the diversity of the blockchain ecosystem itself: from institutional finance and regulation to builders, communities, creators, and market infrastructure.

### Quality Over Crowd

One of the most important signals from MENA Blockchain Week 2026 was the quality of the audience.

The event was not designed only around attendance numbers. Its structure brought together founders, executives, regulators, institutional players, investors, exchanges, infrastructure companies, and community leaders.

The campaign generated more than 10M in reach, with 99% positive sentiment and zero brand-safety incidents reported by the organizers.

This combination of scale, audience quality, and controlled positioning helped turn the initiative into a broader signal for Dubai’s blockchain and digital asset market.

### Institutional Representation

MENA Blockchain Week 2026 included strong institutional representation from across the UAE and the broader region.

VARA participated through senior representatives, while Dubai Blockchain Center, Dubai Digital Asset Association, DMCC Crypto Centre, UAE Blockchain & AI Association, MENA Fintech Association, and other organizations helped anchor the event within the region’s institutional landscape.

The presence of major exchanges and blockchain companies also reinforced Dubai’s position as a meeting point between regulation, capital, infrastructure, and global Web3 communities.

### A Regulated-Market Initiative

MENA Blockchain Week 2026 operated within Dubai’s regulatory framework.

The presence of VARA and other institutional partners gave the initiative an important layer of credibility, especially at a time when the blockchain industry is moving from experimentation toward regulated adoption.

The event showed that Dubai’s blockchain ecosystem is not only about speed and growth, but also about structure, compliance, and trust.

### The Coalition Behind the Week

The initiative was organized by SkyNet X Solutions, with Hadron Founders Club as a founding partner and Dubai Business Events as destination partner.

Strategic and ecosystem partners included Binance, Polygon, Dubai Blockchain Center, Dubai Digital Asset Association, UAE Blockchain & AI Association, MENA Fintech Association, Ghaf Labs, UNBOX Community, Dubai Ethereum Community Hub, GDG Sharjah, AI3 Labs, and others.

Media and communication partners helped extend the initiative’s reach across regional and international audiences.

### A Citywide Model for the Future

The most important element of MENA Blockchain Week 2026 was not only the number of events or attendees, but the model itself.

Instead of concentrating the industry in one conference hall, the initiative activated Dubai as a distributed blockchain venue. This reflected how the industry actually works: through communities, side events, private meetings, technical sessions, regulatory conversations, investor discussions, and informal trust-building.

In that sense, MENA Blockchain Week became more than a blockchain event. It became a citywide mechanism for ecosystem coordination.

### Looking Ahead

MENA Blockchain Week 2026 was launched as a platform designed to scale beyond one edition.

According to the organizers, future editions are planned across Dubai and Abu Dhabi, with expansion into new verticals such as MENA AI Week and cross-border collaboration with blockchain and AI weeks around the world.

The first edition made a clear statement: the future of blockchain in the region will not be built only through products or protocols. It will be built through cities, institutions, communities, regulation, capital, and trust.

For one week, Dubai showed what that future can look like when an entire city becomes part of the infrastructure.

title: Global Tech Weekend Tbilisi 2026: How a Citywide Festival United the Region’s Tech Ecosystem
excerpt: Global Tech Weekend Tbilisi 2026 brought more than 10,000 attendees, 150 brands, and 200 speakers to Georgia’s capital, turning the city into a platform for technology, culture, startups, investment, and cross-sector collaboration.
content:
## From June 19-21, Global Tech Weekend Tbilisi 2026 Hosted the Region's Largest Technology Celebration

The event officially began on Friday, June 19, with a series of workshops, lectures, and private working sessions hosted by partner organizations in coworking spaces, universities, and cultural institutions across the city.

### More Than 150 Brands and 200 Speakers Under One Roof

The flagship event took place on June 20 at Factory Tbilisi, where five stages operated throughout the day, hosting speakers from some of the world's most recognizable companies and organizations, including Meta, Fuckup Nights, Monday.com, Dolce & Gabbana, and many others.

> "The strength of our movement lies in its diversity. Global Tech Weekend Tbilisi did not limit itself to a narrow technology niche. Instead, it expanded beyond traditional tech and embraced adjacent industries. This was reflected in the diversity of our attendees as well. In our pavilions, you could find Web3 developers and social media influencers alongside sports analysts and fashion commentators. We gave a platform to everyone who had valuable insights from their profession to share with a wider audience. We can confidently say that we managed to unite the region's technology ecosystems on an unprecedented scale, and this is only the beginning." says Mariam Chikadze, Head of Marketing at Global Tech Weekend.

One of the main achievements of the flagship event was its ability to bring together professionals from vastly different industries and create space for new conversations and collaborations. Dedicated networking zones allowed guests to exchange ideas, build relationships, and explore future partnerships in a relaxed environment.

June 19-21, 2026 marked a major milestone for Georgia's technology ecosystem. During these three days, Global Tech Weekend welcomed more than 10,000 attendees from around the world to Tbilisi, creating opportunities for knowledge exchange, inspiration, and collaboration across industries.

But this was far from a traditional festival where people gather in a single venue and just watch presentations. Instead, Global Tech Weekend unfolded across multiple locations throughout the city, combining conferences, workshops, networking experiences, and cultural encounters. Alongside professional programming, international guests were able to explore Tbilisi, connect with local communities, and experience the city's unique character firsthand.

Some sessions demanded deep concentration, diving into highly technical topics and emerging technologies. Others offered a faster pace, particularly on the startup-focused stages, where more than 60 startups pitched their ideas to world-class investors between keynote presentations and panel discussions.

The expo areas added another layer to the experience. Visitors explored art installations, immersive exhibitions, and interactive creative projects throughout the venue. By integrating cultural and artistic experiences into a technology-focused event, GTWT created an environment that appealed not only to innovators and entrepreneurs, but also to audiences seeking inspiration through art and creativity.

### More Than 10 Industries United at One Event

Global Tech Weekend Tbilisi brought together experts and organizations from a wide range of sectors:

• Artificial Intelligence & Deep Tech

• Fintech & Banking

• Innovation, Web3 & Blockchain

• Urban Innovation & Architecture

• Gaming & eSports

• Sports

• Creative & Fashion Technologies

• Tourism & Hospitality

• Health Technologies

• Media & Digital Marketing

• Art & Culture

Organizers plan to expand the program even further in future, introducing additional industries and creating an even more comprehensive platform for innovation, entrepreneurship, and cross-sector collaboration.

### Closing Events and Looking Ahead

The final day of the festival, June 21, offered participants an opportunity to slow down, reflect, and strengthen the connections formed during the previous two days. The program featured informal business meetings, cultural experiences, and the official closing ceremony at Kiketi Farm.

During the ceremony, organizers thanked more than 150 partners for their support and shared their vision for the movement's future, both locally and internationally.

Global Tech Weekend was originally founded in Los Angeles in 2024 and expanded in Tbilisi by 2025. This year's edition marked the second consecutive time the movement has brought together the largest technology gathering in the Caucasus and Central Asia.

title: Daria Barkova: Art Profiling Turns the Inner World Into a Visual Map
excerpt: Daria Barkova - creator of Art Profiling and The Path of the Lemon, on visual identity, personality analysis, entrepreneurship, AI, and why true individuality begins with the right to be yourself.
content:
### 1. What is Art Profiling, and how is it different from a classical portrait or psychological testing?

Art Profiling is a method of visual personality profiling, where I create an individual artwork as a precise visual instrument that reflects a person’s inner structure at a specific moment in their life: their agency, priorities, limitations, inner conflicts, and potential for transformation.

Unlike a classical portrait, which captures appearance and sometimes character through symbolism or mood, Art Profiling does not depict a person literally. It is not a “similar-looking portrait,” but a metaphorical map of the inner world. The artwork becomes a mirror in which a person recognizes themselves more deeply than through words.

Unlike standard psychological testing — questionnaires, MBTI, Big Five, and so on — Art Profiling does not work through verbal answers, which are often influenced by social desirability. It works through image and metaphor. An image bypasses rational control and speaks directly to the unconscious. It captures not only what a person already understands about themselves, but also what is only beginning to emerge.

It is a living instrument: the artwork can be interactive, like The Tree of Life with magnets, and it continues to work with the person after it has been created — provoking recognition, inner dialogue, and internal shifts.

### 2. How did you come to the idea of using art as a tool for personality analysis?

This idea was born from many years of observing the same phenomenon in my work with entrepreneurs and top managers.

For many years, I worked in HR, personality profiling, and with founders and executives at moments when they clearly understood that change was necessary, but could not yet see or feel that change. They had readiness, but they did not have an image. They lacked form.

Words, tests, charts, and reports helped on the intellectual level, but rarely reached the point of a deep internal shift. A person could understand everything rationally, while the body and the unconscious continued to live according to old patterns.

At some point, I realized that an image works faster and deeper than an explanation. An image bypasses the resistance of the rational mind and immediately speaks to the part of us responsible for self-recognition.

That is how Art Profiling was born. I began translating the results of profiling into a visual metaphor — precise, personal, and created specifically for this person at this particular moment in their journey. Not an abstract artwork “about a lemon,” but a specific visual instrument that makes visible their inner structure, agency, limitations, and growth points.

Art here is not the artist’s self-expression and not decoration. It is a working instrument of transformation, as precise as a map or a navigation system.

At first, these were experiments with clients. Later, they became a full methodology, reflected, for example, in my series The Path of the Lemon.

### 3. Can you really see a person’s character through visual images?

Yes, you can. And sometimes even more deeply than through many traditional methods.

Character is not a set of static traits, but a living system: priorities, fears, motivations, boundaries, decision-making patterns, and inner conflicts. A large part of this system lies beyond what a person is ready or able to describe verbally.

In Art Profiling, I rely on a complex analysis: personality profiling, metaphors that resonate with this particular person, their story, values, and current context. Then all of this is translated into a precise visual language.

An image works as a powerful catalyst for recognition. When a person looks at their artwork, an instant resonant recognition happens — on the level of the body, emotions, and the unconscious. Clients often say: “I felt this, but I could not formulate it.” Or: “This is me, even though I have never described myself this way.”

A visual image bypasses the censorship of the rational mind and social masks.

It shows not who a person “presents” themselves to be, but how they are structured internally at this moment. For example, in The Path of the Lemon, the lemon is not simply a fruit, but a metaphor for resilience, acidity as inner strength, and resistance to being averaged out. Every element of the composition — color, texture, interaction between objects, inscriptions — carries meaning and reflects specific aspects of personality.

Of course, it is not a “photograph of character” in an absolute sense. It is an instrument that captures the current state and, at the same time, opens a path toward transformation. Character is not static — and the artwork reflects that too.

### 4. What do you want to reflect in your art?

In my art, I want to reflect a person’s inner truth at a specific moment in their journey — the structure that is difficult to see in the mirror or hear in words.

I am not striving for beauty for beauty’s sake, and I do not create decorative paintings. Every art object in The Path of the Lemon is a precise visual profile. It reflects:

Where a person is internally right now — their current agency, inner supports, and limitations;

What forces and priorities drive them — what I call “acidity,” meaning resilience that does not dissolve into the environment;

What transformations are already maturing and ready to appear;

How they interact with the world — with chaos, opportunities, limitations, and their own nature.

I want the artwork to become a mirror that is more honest than habitual self-perception. I want the person to recognize in it not an idealized image, but a real map of their inner system. I want it to provoke not admiration, but recognition and a shift — when it suddenly becomes visible what exactly is blocking them, and what is already ready to become a resource.

Ultimately, I want to reflect possibility — the transition from “readiness for change” to a clear, visible image of that change. So that after encountering the artwork, a person does not leave with the question “Who am I?” but with the feeling: “Now I see where and how to move.”

This is not art for a gallery. It is an instrument of visual self-realization.

![Image alt text](/media/content/daria-barkova-art-profiling-turns-the-inner-world-into-a-visual-map/image-01.jpg)

### 5. Have there been cases when your Art Profiling radically changed someone’s perception of themselves?

Yes, there have been such cases, and they are exactly why I continue doing this work.

One of the most vivid examples was the head of a large company who came to me during a period of deep burnout and with the feeling: “I have already done everything — but what comes next?” Based on the profiling results, we created his artwork, Under the Sign of Unpredictability, with a reference to Taleb’s Black Swan.

On the canvas, a golden swan appeared against a black background, with lemons in its plumage — a symbol that what he had considered his “chaos and failures” was actually his unique strength: the ability to turn unpredictability into an advantage.

When he saw the finished work, his face literally changed. He was silent for a long time, and then he said: “All my life I thought I was too risky and unsystematic. But in reality, I am someone who has long been living in a world where others are only just learning how to navigate.”

That artwork became an anchor point for him. A few months later, he completely reconsidered the company’s strategy, introduced new approaches to innovation, and, according to him, for the first time in many years felt not like a “burned-out veteran,” but like a person who was exactly in his element.

There were other stories as well: a female leader who saw in her artwork The Lemon of Knowledge. A New Eden confirmation of her right to step away from collective noise and create her own space — and this gave her the courage to launch her project. Or an entrepreneur who, through The Tree of Life, finally saw that time is not about deadlines, but about the quality of inner transformations, and radically changed his approach to management and life.

Art Profiling works precisely because the artwork does not tell a person who they “should” be.It shows who they already are on a deep level. And this recognition often becomes a catalyst for a powerful internal shift.

### 6. What does the process of creating an artwork look like?

The process of creating an Art Profiling artwork is always collaborative, deeply personal, and consists of several stages.

**1. Deep profiling**

We begin with a detailed conversation. I do not simply ask questions — I listen not only to the words, but also to how the person speaks, what metaphors they use, where pauses appear, and where the voice changes. I use my skills as an HR profiler and psycholinguist. We explore the current request, inner structure, key priorities, fears, support points, and what is already ready for transformation.

**2. Finding the central metaphor**

Based on the material gathered, I find the precise visual image that will become the heart of the artwork. In The Path of the Lemon, it is almost always connected to the lemon as a symbol of individuality, resilience, and authenticity, but each time it appears differently — through composition, color, texture, and additional symbols such as a swan, a tree, a map, a mask, and so on.

**3. Creating and approving the sketch**

I show the client a preliminary sketch or description of the composition. It is important that the person feels resonance. Sometimes important insights already appear at this stage.

**4. Material embodiment**

I work in mixed media: canvas, acrylic, plaster, relief elements, and sometimes interactive details, such as magnets in The Tree of Life. This is not a quick illustration — the artwork is created in layers, with attention to texture, light, and volume. Every element carries meaning: color, the position of lemons, inscriptions in Russian or Italian, and the interaction between objects.

**5. Transfer and integration**

When the artwork is ready, we meet again. I do not simply hand over the piece — we “read” it together. The person shares what they see and feel, and often the strongest shifts happen at this moment. The artwork remains with the client as a constant visual anchor and a tool for further inner work.

The whole process takes from several weeks to a month and a half, depending on complexity. It is always individual — there are no two identical artworks, just as there are no two identical people.

### 7. How do entrepreneurs use the results of Art Profiling in business?

Entrepreneurs use Art Profiling as a powerful strategic and managerial tool that translates inner states and systemic patterns into a clear visual format.

Here is how it works in practice.

Personal navigation for the leader. The artwork becomes a constant visual anchor. For example, Under the Sign of Unpredictability, an homage to Taleb, helps an entrepreneur stop being afraid of Black Swans and begin seeing them as an area of strength. A leader who once perceived his tendency toward risk as a weakness began, after working with the artwork, to consciously build the company’s strategy around the ability to operate in conditions of high uncertainty.

Corporate culture and team dynamics. Works such as Taste of the Lemon as a Right, a map of corporate culture, are used as tools for aligning values. Here, the lemon acts as a mediator between a person’s inner structures and the reality of business. Entrepreneurs place such works in offices or use them during strategic sessions so that the team can better understand what “our acidity” means — our authenticity, boundaries, and priorities.

Complex decision-making. The Tree of Life (I Govern the World) helps rethink the relationship with time: measuring it not by deadlines, but by the quality of inner transformations. Many entrepreneurs, after working with this artwork, reconsider KPIs, motivation systems, and their own personal leadership.

Transformation after crisis. As in the story I mentioned earlier: after deep profiling and the creation of a personal map, a leader was able to unite the team, come out of crisis, and take the company to a new level — including through digital transformation.

Ultimately, Art Profiling helps entrepreneurs make the invisible visible: inner structure, hidden resources, tension points, and zones of growth. The artwork works as a constant “mirror coach,” reminding you who you really are and where you truly need to move — both in business and in life.

### 8. What qualities unite the most successful entrepreneurs you have analyzed?

Among all the entrepreneurs and leaders I have worked with through Art Profiling and classical profiling, there are several key qualities that consistently repeat among those who reach a truly high level.

1. High “acidity” — in the sense of The Path of the Lemon. This means inner resistance to being averaged out and standardized. They do not try to “please everyone” and do not dissolve into collective norms. They have a clear inner position that they are willing to defend, even when it is not immediately convenient or profitable.

2. The ability to turn uncertainty into a resource. Almost all of them live in the logic of the Black Swan, as in the artwork Under the Sign of Unpredictability. What others perceive as chaos and risk is their natural habitat. They do not wait for stability — they build their strength on the ability to work with unpredictability.

3. A deep connection with their own inner structure. The successful entrepreneurs I have profiled have a developed capacity for self-reflection. They are not afraid to look at their shadows, limitations, and “dark” sides. That is why works such as The Tree of Life or Individuation resonate so strongly with them — they are ready to “break the egg” in order to reach a new level.

4. Orientation toward meaning and long-term transformation. They measure time not by the calendar and not by deadlines, but by the quality of internal and external change, as in The Tree of Life (I Govern the World). Money and results matter, but they understand that the real foundation lies in personal qualities, located in the “crown” of the tree, as in The Tree of Knowledge. 21st Century.

5. High agency and responsibility for choice. Even under strong constraints, they see points of control and opportunities for maneuver. They are captains of their own ships, able to align their vision with the team while not losing their own course.

Of course, each person is unique — and that is exactly what I show in my works. But these qualities create a common pattern: resilience without rigidity, courage without recklessness, and deep inner authorship of one’s own life.

### 9. Which archetypes do you most often see among entrepreneurs and leaders?

I see them through the prism of both my methodology The Path of the Lemon and Jungian psychology — Carl Gustav Jung and his followers, including James Hillman, Marie-Louise von Franz, and others. These are the main archetypes that appear consistently.

1. The Swan — Golden Swan / Black Swan → The Hero + The Trickster + The Self. 
In Jungian terms, this is a strong manifestation of the Self — the center of the psyche that integrates opposites: chaos and order, darkness and light. At the same time, there is also the Trickster — the one who breaks old rules and brings something new through unpredictability. The Swan entrepreneur has already “crossed the line” and lives in a space where others are still afraid to enter. This is the archetype of transformation through crisis.

2. The Lemon → Individuation + Shadow + Animus / Anima in a mature form.
The lemon is a vivid embodiment of the process of individuation. It is the rejection of the Persona — the social mask, the “sweet,” averaged image — and the acceptance of one’s Shadow: acidity, sharp edges, authenticity. The lemon symbolizes the Animus for women or the Anima for men in their authentic, non-adapted form — the part of the psyche that demands the right to be itself, even when it is inconvenient.

3. The Tree of Life / The Tree of Knowledge → The Self + The Wise Old Man / The Great Mother.
This is a classical Jungian archetype of the Self as a holistic image of the psyche. The tree is the axis of the world, Axis Mundi, connecting the roots — the material, the unconscious, money — and the crown — spirit, meaning, personal qualities. In The Tree of Knowledge. 21st Century, the tension between the collective unconscious and the individual path is especially visible — a typical theme of Jungian maturity.

4. The Captain of the Ship → The King / Ruler + The Wise Old Man.
This is the manifestation of the King, or the Ruler, in its positive aspect — the one who holds space, builds hierarchy, and at the same time remains part of the system. The Wise Old Man is also present here as a guide who is able to listen to the wind and the waves — the unconscious.

5. The Hero of Individuation, breaking the egg → The Classical Hero + The Archetype of Rebirth.
This is the direct Jungian Hero passing through the stage of death and rebirth. Breaking the egg is the destruction of the old Persona and the emergence into a new quality. It is very close to the archetype of the Hero’s Journey, described by Joseph Campbell, who developed Jung’s ideas further.

These archetypes are not static — they live in the dynamics of individuation. The most successful entrepreneurs I have profiled are in the process of actively integrating these forces: they do not run away from the Shadow, but transform it into a source of energy.

![Image alt text](/media/content/daria-barkova-art-profiling-turns-the-inner-world-into-a-visual-map/image-02.jpg)

### 10. How does art help people make bolder decisions?

Art in the format of Art Profiling helps people make bolder decisions because it makes the invisible visible and turns inner conflict into a clear point of support.

When a person looks at their artwork, deep recognition takes place. Suddenly, they see their real structure — where their true strength is, where the mask is, where fear lives, and where the new version of themselves is already ready to appear. This removes a huge amount of internal resistance.

Specifically:

It reduces fear of the unknown. For example, Under the Sign of Unpredictability shows that unpredictability is not a threat, but your natural environment. A person stops waiting for “stability,” which may never come, and begins to act in uncertainty.

It gives permission to be oneself. Works from The Path of the Lemon — especially The Lemon of Knowledge. A New Eden or Individuation: Without Breaking the World, One Cannot Build the Self — show that “acidity,” sharp edges, and the refusal to be averaged out are not flaws, but a right. When a person internally allows themselves to be inconvenient, they stop holding themselves back in their decisions.

It translates abstract values into a tangible image. In The Tree of Life (I Govern the World), a person sees that they themselves govern their time and transformations. This changes the criteria for decision-making: instead of “What is safer?” the question becomes “What corresponds to my path and my inner structure?”

It launches the process of individuation. As in the painting with the breaking mask and the lemon, art gives the experience that “breaking the egg” is not frightening. On the contrary, it is a necessary step toward a new version of oneself. After such an experience, many clients make decisions they had not dared to make for years: launch a new project, change the direction of a business, say no to toxic partners, or leave their comfort zone.

Art here does not work as inspiration, but as a precise instrument. It removes the gap between knowledge — as the result of experience — and action. A person does not simply “understand” that they need to be braver; they see themselves already existing in this new quality. And when the image exists internally, the decision becomes the natural next step.

### 11. With the development of AI and technology, does art still have a place?

Art does not simply still have a place — in the age of AI, it becomes even more necessary than before.

Technology and artificial intelligence are excellent at data analysis, process optimization, prediction, and scaling. But there are things that AI cannot yet replace and perhaps will never fully replace: Deep self-recognition on the level of the body and the unconscious.

The experience of resonance — when an image precisely touches your inner structure.

The ability to turn abstract insights into a tangible, living reality.

In my project The Path of the Lemon, I already integrate AI into the profiling process — analyzing large volumes of data, behavioral patterns, and linguistic structures. But the final art object is always created by a human for a human. AI helps make profiling more precise and scalable, but the artwork remains handmade. That is where its strength lies.

Art in the future will become a compensatory mechanism of the digital age. The more we are surrounded by algorithms, averaged content, and virtual reality, the stronger the need will be for an authentic, material, non-standard image. The lemon as a symbol of resistance to standardization is a very timely metaphor.

I see Art Profiling as a bridge between technology and the human soul. AI can process thousands of personality parameters, while art transforms those parameters into an experience that changes a person from within. That is why I am now developing a project where The Path methodology is combined with AI — to make deep profiling accessible to thousands of people while preserving its living artistic core.

Art does not compete with technology. It complements technology where the algorithm ends and the human being begins.

### 12. If you could create an Art Profile for a well-known modern entrepreneur, who would it be?

It would probably be Elon Musk — a truly strong and precise contemporary example of a person walking The Path of the Lemon. If I were creating his art profile, it would be one of the most powerful and multi-layered works in the project.

Why does he embody The Path of the Lemon so precisely?

Extreme “acidity” and resistance to standardization. Musk refuses to play by the familiar, dogmatized, and long-outdated rules of industries. He does not “sweeten” his goals to meet the expectations of the market, investors, or society. His approach often causes irritation, criticism, and even ridicule — the classic reaction to a “lemon.” It unsettles and heals at the same time.

Working with Black Swans as a norm. He lives in the logic of Under the Sign of Unpredictability. Constant uncertainty is not an exception for him, but a basic environment. He turns chaos into fuel for development.

High agency and authorship of reality. As in The Tree of Life (I Govern the World), he is literally trying to govern time and the future of humanity: multiplanetary life, neural interfaces, energy. He sees time not as a linear resource, but as a field for radical transformations.

Individuation through constant “breaking of the egg.” Musk has repeatedly broken his own masks and previous identities: from PayPal to Tesla, SpaceX, and xAI. Each time, he moves to a new level, even if to an outside observer it looks insane. He is also able to gather brilliant madmen around him — something that was not available to the geniuses of the past, such as Leonardo da Vinci or Lomonosov.

What would his artwork look like?

The central image would be a huge black swan carrying on its wings vortexes of white, radiant color, turning into stars of personalities ignited by Musk’s genius, intergalactic rockets, and neural networks. Or it could be a giant Tree of Life whose roots go into an intergalactic corridor and black holes at the centers of galaxies, while its crown turns into neural connections. The background would be black space with bright lemon-yellow accents, symbolizing his “acidity” that illuminates the darkness, revealing systems inside imaginary chaos.

The inscription could be: “You have already crossed the line. Now you must carry chaos within you to give birth to dancing stars” — a reference to Nietzsche, whom he admires.

Musk is a modern Chaos that does not simply exist in an anti-dogmatic form, but uses that form as both a weapon and a light for changing civilization. He vividly demonstrates the main idea of the project: true strength is born not from the desire to please everyone, but from deep loyalty to one’s inner nature.

### 13. What is the main insight you would like every viewer to take away after encountering your art?

I want every person who looks at the works from The Path of the Lemon to take away one main insight:

“To be yourself is not a privilege, but a right. And this right must be consciously claimed.”

You do not have to be sweet, convenient, and understandable to everyone. You do not have to dissolve into the “average person,” who in fact does not exist. Your “acidity” — your unique nature, your sharp edges, your true priorities and boundaries — is not a flaw that needs to be corrected. It is what makes you alive and capable of creating your own path.

I want a person to leave the encounter with the artwork with a deep sense of permission:

Permission to see their real self, without familiar masks.

Permission not to be afraid of their difference.

Permission to turn inner chaos and contradictions into a source of strength.

Permission to govern their own life and time, rather than submit to external rules.

The main insight is recognition: “This is who I am. And I have the right to be exactly this way.” And after that comes action. Because when a person truly sees their inner structure, the decision to move forward becomes natural and much bolder.

title: Global Tech Weekend Tbilisi: How the City Became an Interface for a New Tech Region
excerpt: Global Tech Weekend Tbilisi turned the city into a regional interface for founders, investors, AI teams, fintech operators, Web3 projects, and creative industries — showing how new tech hubs are built through capital, culture, trust, and human connection.
content:
### Global Tech Weekend Tbilisi: How the City Became an Interface for a New Tech Region

For three days, Tbilisi was no longer just a city between Europe, the Caucasus, and Central Asia.

During Global Tech Weekend Tbilisi, it became a point of convergence for people who usually meet in different places: founders, investors, AI teams, fintech operators, creative industries, banks, developers, Web3 projects, and those building the infrastructure for the next technological cycle.

**The main insight from GTWT is that technology no longer exists separately from the city, capital, culture, and trust.**

In the past, conferences often served as showcases for products. Here, the feeling was different: Tbilisi was not trying to present itself simply as a location for an event, but as a new regional hub capable of connecting markets, people, and ideas.

The format played a key role.

Global Tech Weekend was not built around one stage and a few panels, but as a decentralized movement across the city. Side events, workshops, closed-door meetings, investor formats, networking zones, and the main day at Factory Tbilisi created the feeling not of a conference, but of an entire tech week compressed into one weekend.

On the surface, it looked like a large-scale event: stages, speakers, investors, startups, partners, an afterparty, and a cultural program.

But on a deeper level, GTWT revealed several more important shifts.

![Image alt text](/media/content/global-tech-weekend-tbilisi-how-the-city-became-an-interface-for-a-new-tech-region/image-01.jpg)

### AI Has Become the Language of Every Industry

The first is that AI has finally stopped being a topic for a separate panel.

It has become the language spoken by almost every industry. In the creative sector, AI was discussed not as a tool for generating beautiful images, but as a new production layer. In finance, it appeared as part of risk management, onboarding, compliance, and customer experience. In software, it emerged as a factor changing the very economics of development: smaller teams, faster cycles, and greater responsibility placed on product logic.

![Image alt text](/media/content/global-tech-weekend-tbilisi-how-the-city-became-an-interface-for-a-new-tech-region/image-02.jpg)

### Fintech and Web3 Are Growing Up

The second insight is that fintech and Web3 are growing up.

The conversation is becoming less about hype and more about infrastructure: regulation, banks, payments, compliance, tokenization, trust, and institutional partnerships.

For the region, this is especially important. The Caucasus and Central Asia do not have to copy old financial models. They have a chance to build hybrid infrastructure from the start, where digital assets, banking products, and international payment scenarios do not exist separately, but within one system.

![Image alt text](/media/content/global-tech-weekend-tbilisi-how-the-city-became-an-interface-for-a-new-tech-region/image-03.jpg)

### Investors Are Looking at Smart Edges

The third point is that investors are no longer looking only at “large markets,” but also at “smart edges.”

GTWT highlighted this clearly: the future does not have to be born only in San Francisco, London, or Dubai. New ecosystems are becoming interesting precisely because they have less fatigue, more speed, and a greater readiness for unconventional solutions.

In this sense, Tbilisi does not look like a periphery, but like a bridge between Eastern Europe, Central Asia, the Middle East, and global capital.

### Technology Can No Longer Be Separated From Culture

The fourth shift is that technology can no longer be separated from culture.

Alongside AI, venture, and fintech, the program included creative tech, fashion tech, gaming, entertainment, tourism, real estate, and hospitality.

This is an important signal: the next stage of growth will not happen only through code and investment, but also through experience, identity, community, and the urban environment. It is no longer enough for a startup to be technological. It has to be understandable, visible, and embedded in context.

![Image alt text](/media/content/global-tech-weekend-tbilisi-how-the-city-became-an-interface-for-a-new-tech-region/image-04.jpg)

### Networking Has Become the Main Product

The fifth point is that networking has become not a side effect, but the main product.

In a world where almost any information can be found online, the value of offline events has shifted. People come not just to listen to talks. They come to test trust, feel the energy of a team, speak without filters, and find partners who cannot be reached through a cold email.

GTWT built an entire mechanism around this: investor lounges, side events, founder meetings, closed formats, and urban points of attraction.

### Tbilisi as an Organic Stage

The role of Tbilisi itself deserves special attention.

The city turned out to be an organic stage for such an event. It is international enough to bring together different audiences, but still alive and informal enough not to turn a tech forum into a sterile exhibition.

It is easier to talk here, easier to connect, and easier to feel that the ecosystem is still being built — which means you can enter it not as a spectator, but as a participant.

### A New Regional Tech Agenda

Global Tech Weekend Tbilisi showed that the regional tech agenda is becoming increasingly independent.

This is no longer a conversation about how to “catch up” with major markets. It is a conversation about what role the Caucasus, Central Asia, and neighboring ecosystems can play on the new map of technology, capital, and entrepreneurship.

The main takeaway after GTWT is simple: the future does not arrive in one single center.

**It is distributed.**

And the cities that can connect capital, talent, culture, a regulation-friendly environment, and international networks will become the new points of growth.

During these three days, Tbilisi made exactly that kind of statement.

title: Sam Kaploushenko: The Future of Money Is Invisible
excerpt: Sam Kaploushenko - fintech and crypto growth executive on payments, regulations, white-lable infrastructure, AI, trust, and why the next financial revolution will feel almost invisible.
content:
### 1. You've worked across crypto, payments, fintech infrastructure, and business growth. When did you first realize that finance was no longer just about banks?

When I was 5, I already knew I'd be a banker. When I first discovered crypto in 2015 and what it could do, I was certain this was a different financial world - that the classic financial system would never be the same, and that the technology was already ready to offer the world a new financial revolution. Today I realize I wasn't wrong, either as a kid or at 25. When I saw how people actually move money and what banks were offering, it became clear that finance is infrastructure - and a bank is just one of its providers.

### 2. People used to separate crypto and traditional finance. Do you think that division still exists - or are we already living in a hybrid financial world?

The division mostly survives in people's heads and in regulation, not in their behavior. In practice, the user no longer thinks "this is crypto and that's fiat" - they think "I have money and I want to use it." Ten years ago the Bitcoin maximalists talked about a brand-new financial system. I see it more as an evolution - a new stage in the development of finance and technology.

### 3. What do most people still misunderstand about crypto adoption?

That adoption is about speculation and the token price. Real adoption actually happens quietly - when crypto stops being an investment object and becomes a way to get something done: receive a salary, send money to family, pay for something. People come to crypto en masse not for the gains, but because it solves a specific pain faster and cheaper than the alternative.

### 4. Is crypto becoming more mature - or simply becoming better integrated into the old financial system?

Both - and that's the normal path. Maturity shows up precisely in the technology no longer fighting the system and starting to work with it - through licenses, compliance, cards, banking rails. A revolution that wants to replace everything usually loses; a revolution that makes the existing better wins.

### 5. You've seen the industry from different angles: exchange, payments, infrastructure, licensing, growth. Which part of fintech is most misunderstood from the outside?

Compliance and licensing. From the outside it looks like bureaucracy and friction; from the inside it is the product - it determines whether you can move money at all and whether you'll still have access to the rails tomorrow. The "most boring" part of fintech is actually what decides whether a company survives. Today you have no business being in this market if you don't have the technology and the legal side.

### 6. Everyone wants financial products to feel simple. But what is the hidden complexity behind that simplicity?

Behind every "send" button there are dozens of integrations, checks, licenses, and partners the user will never see. Simplicity on the screen is always someone's enormous work under the hood: payment routing, AML checks, liquidity, agreements with banks. The simpler a product looks, the more complex it usually is inside.

### 7. What does "zero-stress payments" mean to you - not as a slogan, but as a real user experience?

It's when a person doesn't think about the payment at all - it just happens, and there's no anxious "will it arrive, will it get blocked, how much will I lose on fees." The absence of stress is predictability: you know in advance what will happen and when. A truly good payment experience is one you don't notice.

### 8. Where do companies usually fail when they try to build payment products?

They underestimate the "invisible" part - compliance, relationships with banks, handling edge cases - and overestimate the beauty of the interface. Payments look simple as long as everything works; all the real complexity is in what happens when something goes wrong. Most companies fail not on the happy path, but on refunds, disputes, freezes, and regulation.

### 9. Is the future of fintech about building new financial products - or making existing financial rails invisible?

More the latter. Most of the rails already exist - the task is to remove them from the user's view and from their mind. The winners won't be those who build yet another bank, but those who make money so embedded in ordinary actions that no one remembers the payment itself.

### 10. White-label fintech is quietly becoming a huge part of the industry. Why do more companies want infrastructure instead of building everything themselves?

Because building payment infrastructure from scratch means years, licenses, and huge money - and it's almost never what a company is actually good at. A business wants the outcome - cards, payments, wallets for its customers - not years of wrestling with regulation. White-label lets you launch in weeks what would otherwise take years, and focus on your own product and customers.

### 11. At what point does fintech infrastructure become a competitive advantage?

When it lets you move faster than everyone else - launching products, entering markets, and onboarding partners in the time it takes competitors just to gather their paperwork. Infrastructure stops being a mere "cost" and becomes an advantage the moment it turns into speed. Whoever owns the rails sets the pace for everyone riding on them.

### 12. What should founders understand before entering regulated fintech markets?

That regulation isn't an obstacle at the start but a permanent condition of the game - and you have to build for it from day one, not "once we grow." Licenses, compliance, and bank relationships will determine both your speed and your very ability to develop. And one more thing: this is a long game - the winners aren't the fastest, but those who can go the distance. I said in an interview once that serious licenses are part of a strategy spanning at least five years.

### 13. Do you think regulation is slowing innovation - or forcing the industry to become more serious?

Both - but in the long run, it forces the industry to grow up. Yes, it slows things down, sometimes painfully. But it's regulation that filters out the fraudsters and fly-by-night players and makes it possible for an ordinary person to trust a product with their money. There's no mass market without trust, and there's no trust without rules.

### 14. In emerging markets, fintech often solves real pain, not just convenience. What do these markets understand better than developed economies?

They understand that access to money isn't a given. Where the banking system is weak, inflation is high, and sending money to family is expensive and slow, fintech isn't a "convenient app" - it's a necessity. That's why products take root faster and deeper in emerging markets: they close a real need rather than making something already convenient slightly more convenient.

### 15. You've worked with crypto and fintech businesses across different regions. Which market feels underestimated right now?

The underestimated markets are the ones that combine a young, mobile-first population, weak legacy banks, and real pain around cross-border payments. There's no burden of legacy systems there, so the new gets adopted immediately and powerfully - which makes them more interesting than the "obvious" mature markets.

### 16. What separates a fintech company that scales globally from one that stays local?

Infrastructure and compliance built for many jurisdictions rather than for a single country. A local company builds for one market and hits a wall at the very first border; a global one thinks from the start in terms of licenses, partners, and rails across regions. The difference isn't in the product - it's in the foundation.

### 17. We often talk about financial freedom. But what does financial freedom actually mean in a world of compliance, AML, banks, licenses, and infrastructure?

Financial freedom isn't the absence of rules - it's the absence of friction. Freedom is when you can store, send, and spend your money however you want, while the entire machinery of compliance and licenses works for you, invisibly. Real freedom is born not where there are no rules, but where the rules are followed so well that you don't feel them.

### 18. In the next five years, will people care whether they use crypto, fiat, or tokenized assets - or will the payment layer become invisible?

The layer will become invisible. People don't care what protocol carries their message in a messenger app - and it'll be the same with money. In five years, "is this crypto or fiat?" will sound as strange as "what protocol did my email go over?" does today. What matters is the outcome, not the rail.

### 19. What role will AI play in fintech: better risk management, better personalization, or a completely new financial interface?

First, risk and compliance, because that's where the return is most obvious and measurable: AI catches fraud and processes checks at a scale humans can't reach. Next, personalization. But in the long run the biggest change is a new interface: you simply say what you want to do with your money, and the system does it. AI will go from being a tool to being the way we interact with finance.

### 20. What trend in fintech looks overhyped today but may become inevitable later?

A good example is asset tokenization and, in a sense, CBDCs themselves: today there's a lot of noise around them and little real use, but the underlying idea - that any value becomes programmable and instantly transferable - is almost certainly inevitable. The hype runs ahead of the infrastructure; that's normal. What's overhyped today and inevitable tomorrow is often the same thing, just at different stages.

### 21. What has this industry taught you about trust?

That trust is the real product in finance. People hand you the most sensitive thing they have - their money - and that trust is earned over years and lost in a single failure. That's why all the boring stuff - compliance, security, reliability - is actually what matters most: the technology is just a tool, but trust is the business itself.

### 22. Final REVELATIONS question: **What is something you understand about the future of money that the rest of the world will only realize later?**

That money will stop being a place you "go into" and become a function built into everything around us. We'll stop "using finance" the same way we stopped "going online" - it's just everywhere. The future of money is that it becomes invisible: not an app, not an account, not a bank, but a property of any action. Whoever builds for that world now is the one who'll define what it looks like.

Global Tech Weekend Tbilisi, the region’s most expansive technology movement, is returning this year with an even more influential lineup. **Google, Nike, Dolce & Gabbana, Amazon, Amber, Fuckup Nights**: the list goes on, ultimately bringing together over 200 speakers. On June 20, GTWT 2026 will host these guests at their flagship event, spread across five stages at Factory Tbilisi.

Have you ever wondered about the techniques behind business analysis at one of the world’s most celebrated [fashion houses](https://www.dolcegabbana.com/en-tr/)? Or what the daily routine is like inside the office of a [digital management platform](https://monday.com/) used to coordinate your team’s tasks? Are you interested in how internationally renowned [angel investors](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ronald-weissman-36a3841/) perceive Georgia’s startup potential? Perhaps you want to attend a keynote from a [lecturer at Stanford University](https://www.linkedin.com/in/bretwaters/) and hear personal stories from the famous Silicon Valley. You can experience all this and more at the main technology event of the year: Global Tech Weekend Tbilisi 2026.

> "We have doubled the number of invited speakers this year. The list is comprised of both exceptional local professionals who have been creating innovation and new knowledge in Georgia for years, as well as representatives of world-famous brands who have contributed significantly to shaping global business and cultural trends. We plan to provide these individuals with a stage in traditional conference settings, while also bringing them into informal networking zones so that Global Tech Weekend guests have the opportunity to meet them personally," says Nia Resulidze, Head of Speakers and Operations.


## Who, where, and when will you see at Global Tech Weekend Tbilisi 2026?

The events are spread across three days, with GTWT 2026 hosting guests at various locations provided by partner companies throughout Tbilisi. 

**On the first day**, June 19, more than 80 events are planned, including workshops, conferences, closed working meetings, and lectures. The full program is available at [luma.page](https://luma.com/calendar/manage/cal-jEDFQzrLAKPYj9U).

**The flagship event** will take place on Saturday, June 20, in the former Coca-Cola factory building. Across the five different stages at [Factory Tbilisi](https://factorytbilisi.com/), you will have the opportunity to see:

### Monika Bielskyte
Founder of Protopia Futures and Nike’s first Futurist in Residence. As a foresight practitioner, she develops resilient future strategies informed by science, technology, and lived human experience. Monika has worked with clients such as Disney/Marvel, Google, Microsoft, and the BBC, and she frequently lectures at institutions like CERN and Rockefeller University.

### Dot Lung
A social media strategist who bridges the gap between human behavior and digital culture. She began her marketing career on MySpace and now creates campaigns for Meta, Adobe, and Wix. Dot is known in digital marketing circles as the "Mother of Dragons" for developing the "Dragon Strategy" during the evolution of social media.

### Luciano Freitas 
Head of Aftermoon and an innovative entrepreneur who applies mathematical precision to strategy and marketing to drive company growth. A global marketing expert with over $10 billion in impact, he has held leadership positions at Airbnb, Uber, and Hotmart. Luciano is also a neuroscientist and leadership specialist who provides consulting for global giants such as Pfizer, Deloitte, and Danone.

### Pepe Villatoro 
A serial entrepreneur and co-founder of Fuckup Nights. The organization he created is a global community that teaches people how to reframe failure as a tool for innovation. Fuckup Nights has visited more than 70 countries to date, sharing its unique stories. Pepe has also successfully managed the rapid growth of unicorn companies such as WeWork and Deel.

### Mike Fischer 
A legendary executive in interactive entertainment who held C-level leadership positions at Amazon, Microsoft, and Square Enix America. He shaped the publishing strategy for iconic franchises including: Fortnite, Final Fantasy, Tomb Raider, and Halo. Currently, Mike is a General Partner at the gaming industry venture fund, Firstpoint VC.

### Thomas Kolster 
A global authority on marketing and sustainable business whom Forbes has called a "climate change agent." He coined the term "Goodvertising" and introduced a methodology in his book, "The Hero Trap," that helps brands create real impact. Thomas has provided consulting for companies including Meta, Adidas, IKEA, and P&G.

Alongside international speakers, guests will also hear from representatives of standout Georgian brands. This approach makes it possible to tackle local challenges by integrating international experience, which remains one of the primary missions of the movement.

**The third day** will bring together cultural experiences and informal business meetings, with Global Tech Weekend Tbilisi 2026 finally concluding on the evening of June 21 with a closing ceremony and a cocktail party.

Information about events and speakers is subject to updates. For the latest news, visit the official social media channels of GTWT 2026: [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/global.tech.weekend.tbilisi?utm_source=ig_web_button_share_sheet&igsh=ZDNlZDc0MzIxNw==), [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/globaltechweekendtbilisi), [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/globaltechweekendtbilisi/?viewAsMember=true)

title: Global Tech Weekend Tbilisi Returns on June 19-21
excerpt: On a Mission to Accelerate Regional Transformation: Global Tech Weekend Tbilisi Returns on June 19-21
content:
This summer, Georgia will host a wide range of technology, cultural, educational, and business events. Global Tech Weekend Tbilisi 2026 stands out as the platform where all of these worlds intersect. Returning for its biggest edition yet, the region's leading technology movement is expected to welcome more than 10,000 attendees across three days.

From June 19 to 21, venues across Tbilisi will become hubs for learning, collaboration, innovation, and new business opportunities. Whether participants come from startups, established companies, investment funds, creative industries, academia, or the public sector, they can expect to leave with new insights, valuable connections, and fresh inspiration. The scale and diversity of the program are what make this promise possible.

### What exactly is Global Tech Weekend Tbilisi 2026?

It is a city-wide series of networking events, lectures, workshops, conferences, and cultural experiences that brings together globally recognized brands, industry leaders, founders, investors, creators, and innovators.
The scale of GTWT 2026 is best illustrated by the numbers:

- 200+ speakers
- 150+ companies
- Item three
- 300+ investors
- 80+ events
- 1 flagship event at Factory Tbilisi

> "Compared to last year, we are hosting twice as many international guests, and there are clear reasons behind this decision. We want the Georgian audience to meet the people who are driving some of the world's most influential projects. We know that local tech ecosystems cannot evolve without synchronizing with global experience and staying connected to international trends. As regional transformation remains one of our main goals, we believe that knowledge exchange is one of the most powerful ways to achieve it." says Jaba Kikvidze, Co-Founder of the movement.

Due to the diverse nature of the program, events will take place across multiple locations throughout the city.

### • June 19 (Friday) | Side-events Day:
On the opening day, you will probably see GTWT 2026 badges all across Tbilisi because events will be hosted by partner companies in hotels, co-working spaces, universities, and cultural institutions throughout the whole city.

More than 80 events are scheduled for this day alone, including workshops, conferences, private working sessions, networking gatherings, and educational talks. The full event schedule is available on [luma.page](https://luma.com/calendar/manage/cal-jEDFQzrLAKPYj9U).

### • June 20 (Saturday) | Main Day:
[Factory Tbilisi](https://factorytbilisi.com/), the iconic former Coca-Cola facility that has become one of the city's most recognizable creative hotspots, will host the main event of GTWT 2026.

For one day, the venue will be transformed into sectored pavilions hosting conferences, exhibitions, networking experiences, and interactive activities.

Guests will be welcomed from 11:00 AM and participate in programming until 11:00 PM. The conference program will focus on ten major themes: 
- Artificial Intelligence & Deep Tech
- Fintech & Banking
- Innovation, Web3 & Blockchain
- Urban Innovation & Architecture
- Gaming & eSports
- Creative & Fashion Technologies
- Tourism & Hospitality
- Health Technologies
- Media & Digital Marketing
- Art & Culture

Alongside keynote presentations, panel discussions, and fireside chats, attendees will have access to a variety of networking spaces, experiential zones, and relaxation areas designed to encourage meaningful interactions and help with cozy rest throughout the day.

In addition to the conferences, Factory Tbilisi will feature:
- Innovation, Technology & Expo Zones
- Networking & Business Connection Areas
- Art Installations & Interactive Experiences
- Entertainment & Sports Activities
- Live Football Match Broadcasts
- Food & Beverage Areas
- Relaxation Spaces

The diversity of experiences ensures that every attendee, regardless of industry or background, can find opportunities that match their interests.

### • June 21 (Sunday) | Cultural Experiences & Closing Ceremony:
The final day offers participants an opportunity to slow down, reflect on the previous two days, and continue networking in a more informal setting.

title: David Lolaev: If the Future Is a Track, I Want to Drive First
excerpt: David Lolaev - racing-minded entrepreneur on business as Formula 1, human competition, AI, digital twins, and why freedom is worth more than any finish line.
content:
### 1. People often say business is a marathon. But you’re connected to racing. Today, is business a marathon, a sprint, or Formula 1?

Depends from your industry, and from your ambitious. If you want to become champion it's no matter where you fighting for that. You can open a cafe and say that it's too many competitors and you can't win. Or you can find a unique spot and positioning for your business and become stronger than anybody else.

### 2. What do a founder before launching a company and a driver sitting on the starting grid have in common?

I think it's not stages which you can compare. Before you will appear on starting grid you must pass a huge path behind. So every new race for entrepreneur is not about to launch a business, I think it's more about try to climb a new height

### 3. Are you more afraid of extreme speed — or moving too slowly?

I'm more afraid to lose my pace. Because if you are overspeeding above your limits you can't control everything as it must be, so if your "working pace" is higher than your competitiors that a key to win the stage

### 4. The world seems to be accelerating faster than people can adapt. Have you ever felt like life itself was moving faster than you?

I'm trying all my life to be faster than the world around me. And yeah I'm agree with you that things are moving fast nowadays, and every break can be critical for business now. But I always believe that if you can be pioneer somewhere you can win more than others

### 5. Twenty years from now, do you think motorsport becomes fully autonomous — or will people always want a human behind the wheel?

The human racing will never end. It's in our DNA to compete. AI and robotic racing is already exist but it will never replace human challenging and emotions and hardwork of athletes. 

### 6. If you had to choose: driving the fastest car on Earth or piloting the first commercial vehicle on Mars — what would you pick?

If mars vehicle will have enough horse power inside of engine, and if you can promise that Mars has no speed limit cameras), I will choose 2nd option

### 7. Racing used to be about the best driver. Today it’s data, telemetry, analytics. Is business evolving the same way?

Absolutely. You can't imagine how many hundreds of sensors, metrics, and measures racing teams using to make this "fastest driver" happen. Same in business. If you have a blind spots in data, you can't win.

### 8. In 20 years, who will make decisions faster: entrepreneurs or AI?

I can't say it exactly now. Because AI become popular less than 5 years ago and already changed our lives so hard.

### 9. What arrives first: autonomous cities or autonomous racing leagues?

Racing leagues with AI are already there.

### 10. Imagine it’s 2040. What does David Lolaev’s dream garage look like?

Full of old JDM cars :)

### 11. At high speed, you can’t control everything. Is control overrated? 

It always depends from the fact at which speed your control is on same perfect level. If you lose it after 100km/h it's a problem)

### 12. What’s one thing in life that can never truly be delegated?

Parentship

### 13. Some people build companies like machines. Others build ecosystems. Which one are you?

It's a hard question for me. I often think that I'm building a race cars but there are no tracks in the world to open their full potential.

### 14. What feels insane today but will become completely normal in ten years?

Robots I guess. We still looking at them like it's expensive toys but one day it will become absolutely normal that we will see them everywhere.

### 15. Which technology do you think is massively underestimated right now?

Digital twins. It can be next human superpower. When you can create your twins and trust them in delegated tasks.

### 16. Imagine it’s 2045 and you walk into a Museum of the Future. One room features your race car. What does the plaque next to it say?

Was made by free people for dreamers.

### 17. What mistake would the future version of David want to prevent today’s David from making?

Never sell yourself and your freedom even if price is too good.

### 18. If life is a racetrack, what section are you driving through right now: the start, a straight line, a sharp turn, or a risky overtake?

I think we are in 24h Le Mans today going to pit-stop with a lot of damages on the car and we have 30 minutes to deal with repairments of all them, and back to the track to fight for podium

### 19. What scares you more than speed?

Idea that it was the last try of the last race.

### 20. If the future were a race track — would you rather drive first, or wait for someone else to test the road?

Always №1!
